This petition is filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. seeking regular bail in Crime No.8/2023 of Yadagiri Women Police Station, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 376 (3),
376(2)(n) and 506 of IPC and under Sections 4, 6 and 17 of the POCSO Act.

02. Initially the case was registered for the offence punishable under Section 363 of IPC and subsequent to the investigation the offences punishable under Sections 363, 376 (3), 376 (2) (n),
506 of IPC and Section 4, 6 and 17 of POCSO Act, are invoked.

The factual matrix of the prosecution is that the victim in this case was studying in 10th standard in Government School at Wadegeri and the petitioner was used to entice her that he is in love with her and when she refused to do so.
In spite of the same, the petitioner proposed her for a couple of times and threaten her that he would commit suicide if she does not agree to love him.
As such the victim started to love the petitioner.
It is further case of the prosecution that the petitioner asked the victim to elope with him.
When she refused for the same, he threatened her that if she does not accompany him, he would bring disrepute to her parents.

Such being the case, on 24.03.2023 at about 09.00 p.m. when all the family members of the victim were slept, the petitioner went near the house of the victim in a motorcycle bearing its Reg.No.KA-33/B/4473 and the victim came out from her house and though she refused to accompany to him, the accused forced her to accompany him by threatening that if she refused to accompany him, he would commit suicide by consuming poison.

As such the victim had NC: 2024:KHC-K:3287 accompanied him and thereafter, both have went to Yadgiri on a motorcycle and stayed in a rented house of CW.24 in which the accused Nos.2 and 3 were residing.
It is further case of the prosecution that in the said house the accused - petitioner had committed forcible sexual intercourse with the victim between 25.03.2023 to 27.03.2023.

However, complaint is lodged by the mother of the victim girl, the respondent - police after registering the FIR for the offence punishable under Section 363 of IPC, during the course of Sakreppa vs The State Of Karnataka And Anr on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11626096/
2 investigation, traced the accused and the victim on 29.03.2023 and arrested the petitioner and produced before the Trial Judge on 31.03.2023 and thereby remanded to judicial custody.

sentences.text: Aggrieved by the same, the petitioner had approached the learned District and Sessions Judge, at Yadgiri for grant of bail in Special Case No.55/2023.

entities.text: District and Sessions Judge, at Yadgiri
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: However, the learned District Judge, rejected the bail application filed by the petitioner vide order dated 27.09.2023.
Aggrieved by the same, petitioner preferred this bail petition for grant of regular bail.

Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent - State.
05.
It is primary contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that there is an inordinate delay of 02 days in lodging the complaint.
Though the victim eloped along with the petitioner on 24.03.2023, her mother lodged the complaint on 27.03.2023.
Further there was a love affair between the victim and the petitioner.
Such being the case, the prosecution failed to prove the forcible sexual assault made by the petitioner against the victim girl by placing the relevant documents.
According to him the medical document of the victim girl placed by the prosecution depicts that there is no recent sexual intercourse committed to the victim girl.
Neverthless the prosecution also failed to place the authenticated documents to prove the age of the victim girl that she was minor at the time of incident.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.

Per contra, the learned High Court Government Pleader vehemently opposed the bail petition on the ground that as per the prosecution case, the victim girl was aged 15 years 07 months to that effect the prosecution placed the school certificate issued by the Head Master.
Moreover, the statement of the victim, recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. wherein she has clearly stated about the illegal act committed by the petitioner.
Further the parents of the victim have also clearly deposed to that effect.
Hence, there is a prima- facie case made out against the petitioner.
As such he prays to dismiss the bail petition.

07. Having heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned High Court Government Pleader and having perused the documents made available before this Court, including the charge-sheet materials, admittedly there is a love affair between the victim and the petitioner.

The victim voluntarily accompanied the accused and they both stayed at Bidari village Tq; Mudhol NC:
2024:KHC-K:3287 with the help of accused Nos.4 and 5.
The victim had not lodged any complaint to the respondent - police or any other police during her stay with the petitioner.

Further, as rightly contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner, the medical certificate produced by the prosecution depicts that there is no such recent sexual intercourse found on the victim.

Further, on perusal of the age certificate, the same has issued by the Head Master of the School without placing any birth certificate or any authenticated documents issued by the concerned department as laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court and this Court in catena of judgments.

In such circumstances,
without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the considered view that the Sakreppa vs The State Of Karnataka And Anr on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11626096/
3 petitioner has made out a case for grant of regular bail.

sentences.text:
Hence, the following:
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. is allowed.

Consequently, the petitioner/accused No.1 shall be released on bail in connection with Crime No.8/2023 of Yadgiri Women Police Station,
pending on the file of District and Sessions Judge, at Yadgiri, in Special Case No.55/2023, for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 376 (3), 376(2)(n) and 506 of IPC and under Sections 4, 6 and 17 of POCSO Act, on the following conditions:
i) The petitioner shall execute her personal bond for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Only) with two sureties for the likesum to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional Court.
ii) The petitioner shall not tamper with the prosecution witnesses or prevail upon the prosecution witnesses in any manner.
iii) The petitioner shall attend the jurisdiction Court regularly on all dates of hearing and shall cooperate with the investigation authority.
